what: FirstService runs two businesses. FirstService Residential manages residential communities: condominium boards and homeowner associations hire it to handle budgets, maintenance, staff and compliance. FirstService Brands is a group of franchised and company-owned property service businesses including restoration, roofing, painting and fire protection.
customers: Community associations and condominium boards across North America, plus homeowners, insurers and commercial property owners who buy restoration, roofing and fire protection work.
money: Property management contracts for residential communities, largely recurring fee revenue.
Restoration, roofing, painting, fire protection and home services through franchises and company operations.
moat: Residential management contracts renew almost automatically because switching manager is disruptive for a volunteer condominium board, and the business is built on thousands of small contracts rather than a few large ones. The restoration business benefits from insurer relationships: when a building floods, insurers direct work to approved contractors who can mobilise immediately.
risks: The shares trade at about 47 times earnings, which is a high multiple for a services business with 2.6% net margin.
Growth has come substantially from acquiring businesses, which adds goodwill and integration risk.
Restoration revenue depends partly on storms and floods, which is genuinely unpredictable from year to year.
Labour availability and wage inflation affect every one of these businesses directly, since they are people-intensive.
Debt of $1.4B against $154.4M of cash has risen with the acquisition programme.
opportunities: Revenue has grown every year shown, from $3.2B in 2021 to $5.5B in 2025, with trailing revenue of about $5.7B.
The residential management business is genuinely recurring and grows with the number of communities under contract.
Free cash flow of $298.4M is double net income, because amortisation of acquired intangibles depresses reported earnings without consuming cash.
Eight analysts average a $179.00 target, about 17% above the current price.
The property services markets it operates in are highly fragmented, so there is a long runway for consolidating small operators.
watch: Organic revenue growth separate from acquisitions. The acquisition machine works, but the valuation assumes the underlying businesses grow on their own too, and only the organic figure shows that.
